attempts.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9, no LVM/btrfs/package-repo access available), built a snapshot-capable /srv/data using device-mapper directly: a loopback-backed XFS "origin" volume (dmsetup snapshot-origin target on /dev/loop0) mounted at /srv/data, and a COW loopback store (/dev/loop1). Populated /srv/data with app.conf and state/counter.txt, recorded a SHA-256 baseline, then created a dm-snapshot device (data-snap) capturing that exact state. Modified /srv/data (corrupted app.conf, changed counter.txt, added an unexpected file) to simulate real drift, confirmed the snapshot's COW store had preserved the original blocks, mounted the snapshot read-only, verified its checksums matched the baseline, then restored /srv/data by replacing its contents with the snapshot's exact content — post-restore checksums matched the baseline exactly (extra file removed, originals restored byte-for-byte). Made the setup persistent via a systemd oneshot service (data-origin-setup.service) that reattaches the loop devices and recreates the dm-origin table idempotently, plus a srv-data.mount unit, both enabled at boot. Completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol: captured boot_id fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60 and a healthy/matching-baseline data state pre-restart, issued a background `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnection, polled node1 until reachable, confirmed a new boot_id (4f22c5c7-9866-412e-acfd-70785edf7be2) proving an actual restart, and verified full recovery post-restart: dm-origin device reattached, /srv/data remounted automatically, and SHA-256 checksums still match the original baseline exactly. node1 is the cluster's only managed node, so the restart protocol is complete for the full topology.
